projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The spike to 30 connected devices followed by stabilization, combined with zero camera motion late on a Tuesday, strongly indicates a quiet indoor gathering (likely guests or a kids' sleepover) rather than normal household activity or a network anomaly. The pattern suggests everyone is settled off-camera, so no immediate action is needed.

The steady decline and subsequent stabilization of connected devices, combined with zero camera motion over four hours, indicates the household is likely still home but engaged in evening activities outside camera coverage (e.g., backyard or garage) or devices are cycling through sleep mode, rather than a departure or security event.

A steady decline of 7 connected devices over 27 minutes combined with zero camera motion strongly suggests a coordinated group departure (likely guests or the family) bypassing camera triggers, possibly via the garage or back door. This matters because the lack of visual confirmation creates a verification gap, so Steve should check door/garage status if he wasn't expecting anyone to leave.

Presence jumped by ~9 devices between 16:54 and 17:08 while cameras logged no motion, strongly suggesting after-school arrivals or guests entered via a garage or non-motion-triggered door. Confirm if visitors are expected or if entryway sensors need calibration.

Presence sensors show a steady drop of ~5 connected devices between 15:47 and 16:20, but the complete lack of camera motion or door activity during this window suggests either a network connectivity issue affecting presence tracking or a departure outside camera coverage. This discrepancy warrants a quick network status check to rule out sensor drift.

At 3 AM with zero camera activity, the rapid one-minute toggle between 27 and 28 connected devices indicates a network instability or a specific device repeatedly dropping and reconnecting to the Wi-Fi, which could degrade smart home performance over time.

The persistent toggle between 26 and 27 connected devices, paired with zero camera motion or activity, points to a malfunctioning smart device or network glitch rather than human presence. This matters because it is likely causing false presence detection, which could disrupt automations and drain device batteries.

The sustained surge to 27-28 connected devices around 20:42, paired with zero camera motion throughout the evening, strongly suggests a large group of guests or a significant IoT network event occurring entirely within a camera-blind zone. This creates an unmonitored security and safety gap that warrants verification.

The sudden spike to 27-28 devices at 20:42 paired with zero camera motion throughout the evening strongly indicates a large, stationary indoor gathering (likely guests arriving after dinner) rather than normal family activity. This explains the high device count and lack of movement, but you may want to verify cameras weren't accidentally disabled or confirm the event is expected.

The sustained presence of 20-22 devices over four hours with zero camera motion strongly indicates a planned, stationary indoor gathering rather than a transient event or security concern. This suggests normal household routines may be delayed until the guests depart.
